To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HRM system is the key mediating construct that explains how individual employee attributes affect firm performance.
the “strength of the human resource management system” (HRMS) mediates the relationship between human resource management (HRM) practices and organizational effectiveness.
the strength of the HR system is positively related to organizational performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the “strength” of the HRM systems that are responsible for the relationship of HRM practices to firm performance.
how HRM systems can be designed to create a climate of shared understanding that will facilitate the achievement of firm performance goals.
the intermediate linkages that connect the HRM practices of a firm with its performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HRM systems are not the sole determinant of firm performance but that the strength of the HR system does influence the relationship between HR practices and firm performance.
HRM systems that are strong in the way we have defined it are more likely to be associated with higher levels of firm performance.
HRM systems that are strong in the sense of creating a shared climate for interpreting and responding to organizational events will lead to higher levels of organizational effectiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strength of the HR system is a meta-feature that can explain why some organizations are more successful than others in achieving desired HRM outcomes.
a strong HRM system can be used to create a strong organizational climate.
“HRM is not just what HR does, it’s what the firm is.”
The main takeaway from our work is that
a strong HRM system can be a key to the success of an organization.
the HRM–firm performance relationship is moderated by the strength of the HR system.
the “strength” of the HRM climate is an important metafeature of the HRM context that can help explain how HRM practices affect organizational performance.
